UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                   BEFORE THE
                     FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                                         )
Joint Application for Authorization under Section 203 )                 Docket No. EC26-131-000
of the Federal Power Act of NextEra Energy, Inc., et al. )
                                                         )

    PROTEST OF THE CAROLINA INDUSTRIAL GROUP FOR FAIR UTILITY RATES I

         Pursuant to Rules 212 and 2008 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.2008 (2025) and

the Commission’s August 25, 2026 Notice of Extension of Time, the Carolina Industrial Group for

Fair Utility Rates I (“CIGFUR”)1 respectfully protests the application filed on July 15, 2026 (the

“Application”), by NextEra Energy Inc. (“NextEra”) and Dominion Energy, Inc. (“Dominion”)

seeking Commission authorization under sections 203(a)(1) and 203(a)(2) of the Federal Power

Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 824b(a)(1) and (2) (2024), and Part 33 of the Commission’s regulations, 18

C.F.R. pt. 33 (2025), to merge the two companies (the “Transaction”).

    I.      Introduction

         CIGFUR is an affiliated group of non-residential retail customers in Dominion’s North

Carolina service territory. Dominion’s North Carolina service territory serves the smallest

customer base of any of the utility service territories involved in the Transaction, serving fewer

than 150,000 customers. As shown in Exhibit K-1 to the Application, Dominion’s North Carolina

service territory covers large portions of the sparsely populated northeastern portion of the State.

Given this unique service territory and customer base, the Transaction has the potential to

disproportionately, and negatively, impact CIGFUR’s members.



1
 CIGFUR filed a doc-less motion to intervene in this proceeding on September 18, 2026. To date, no party has
opposed CIGFUR's intervention.
           The Application asserts that “the Transaction will not have any adverse effect on

competition, rates, or regulation, and therefore is consistent with the public interest.” As discussed

below, the Application does not adequately demonstrate that the Transaction will not have any

adverse effect on rates. Accordingly, CIGFUR respectfully submits that the Transaction will not

be consistent with the public interest without the Commission imposing the conditions discussed

below to ensure that Dominion and NextEra’s captive customers are held harmless.

    II.      Captive Customers Must Be Held Harmless

          The Commission has held that its main objective in determining whether the Transaction

will have an adverse impact on rates is “to protect captive customers who are served under cost-

based rates that could be adversely affected by a section 203 transaction.”2 The “Applicants

respectfully request that the Commission find that the Transaction does not have an adverse effect

on rates.”3 However, in order to do so, CIGFUR asserts that the Commission must impose the

following three conditions to protect captive customers.

             a. Shareholders Must Bear All Administrative and Transactional Costs

          First, the Commission must condition the Transaction on shareholders of Dominion and

NextEra bearing all costs associated with the Transaction. The Applicants voluntarily “commit,

for a period of five-years after closing of the Transaction, to hold customers harmless from any

Transaction-related costs, which, as set forth in the Commission’s Policy Statement on Hold

Harmless Commitments, include transaction costs.”4 CIGFUR appreciates this voluntarily

commitment, but believes that it should be a binding, enforceable condition imposed on the

Transaction by the Commission.

              b. The Commission Must Ensure No Adverse Customer Class or Jurisdictional
                Impacts

         In determining whether the Transaction is consistent with the public interest, and

specifically whether the Transaction has an adverse effect on rates, the Commission must ensure

that all customers are held harmless, whether they are paying wholesale rates or whether their retail

rates are otherwise impacted by the Transaction, regardless of customer class or jurisdiction.

         First, at the state level, Dominion and NextEra have committed $2.25 billion in shareholder

contributions for near-term bill credits to retail customers, based on the service territory’s pro rata

share of total electric sales.5 However, in Virginia, Dominion has already proposed that the bill

credits would not apply to large customers, including CIGFUR’s members.6 The Commission

should condition approval of the Transaction by requiring the shareholder contributions and that

such contributions be applicable to all customer classes, including to North Carolina’s large load

customers.

         Second, the Commission must consider the jurisdictional impacts of the Transaction to

ensure that North Carolina is not disproportionately burdened. Dominion’s North Carolina service

territory is the smallest involved in the Transaction, containing fewer than 150,000 of Dominion’s

2.8 million customers in Virginia and North Carolina. Furthermore, Dominion has more than 40

gigawatts of new load under contract for service, construction, or engineering,7 none of which are

 located in North Carolina.8 However, Virginia’s load growth is a double-edged sword for

Dominion’s North Carolina ratepayers: while the load growth is reducing North Carolina’s

jurisdictional allocation,9 as discussed in greater detail below, the load growth is also triggering

substantial transmission investments. The Commission should condition approval of the

Transaction on ensuring that North Carolina’s captive customers are not disproportionately

burdened in comparison to Dominion’s much more substantive Virginia service territory.

            c. The Commission Must Ensure Retail Customers are Protected from Ever-
               Increasing Transmission Costs

        Transmission costs in the PJM Interconnection (“PJM”) have more than doubled in the past

decade and now account for approximately 32% of wholesale electricity prices.10 This trend will

only continue as Dominion builds new transmission assets to serve “Data Center Alley” in

Virginia. However, the Application affords no protections to Dominion’s North Carolina ratepayers

from costs associated with Virginia’s load growth. Accordingly, CIGFUR believes that an

Independent Transmission Monitor is warranted for Dominion’s Virginia and North Carolina

service territories.

        While Dominion’s Virginia and North Carolina service territories are located in PJM, the

rapidly increasing costs associated with transmission demonstrate that PJM’s existing processes

are insufficient to protect Dominion’s captive customers. Moreover, both Dominion and NextEra

have affiliates that own and operate, or will operate, transmission assets in PJM. The Commission

 should condition approval of the Transaction by requiring a shareholder-funded Independent

Transmission Monitor for a period of not less than five years.

       The current PJM processes and open access transmission tariff provide insufficient

protections for ratepayers. An Independent Transmission Monitor should provide independent

oversight of transmission planning, development, and cost allocation in the Dominion Zone within

PJM. This role should include ensuring that principles of cost causation are appropriately followed

and protection against affiliate self-dealing, given that both Dominion and NextEra have affiliates

who own transmission assets in PJM.

III.       Conclusion

       As set forth above, Dominion and NextEra have not demonstrated that the Transaction is

consistent with the public interest because they have not demonstrated that the Transaction will

not have any adverse impact on rates.

       WHEREFORE, CIGFUR respectfully requests that the Commission deny the Application

or, in the alternative, approve the Application and impose the conditions discussed in this Protest.

       Respectfully submitted this the 29th day of September 2026.
